topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing complement, addressing its complexity and nomenclature, and setting expectations.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the Complement System and C3 Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the general architecture, nomenclature conventions, and core C3 cleavage mechanism that underpin the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct biochemical pathways that trigger complement activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three primary downstream actions mediated by activated complement to clear infections.

topics.label: Regulation of Complement and Host Protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins that protect host cells from unintended complement activation and lysis.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines how specific genetic and acquired complement deficiencies manifest in distinct clinical pathologies and infection vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens evolve specialized mechanisms to circumvent complement-mediated immunity, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with concluding remarks and a preview of the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
